items.title: FTC Impersonators Are Calling — They Will Threaten to Deactivate Your Phone
items.summary:
The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number.

Scammers are posing as FTC officials and claiming a phone was registered under your name and used for scams in another country. They read off a fake badge ID and threaten to disconnect your phone unless you cooperate. Then they transfer you to a "police officer" who asks for your ID and personal information for a "report." Later they claim you're under arrest and need to send money for a security deposit. None of this is real.

items.title: FBI Impersonation Scams Hit 61,000 Victims — $1.6 Billion Lost
items.summary:
The FBI says scammers impersonating government officials have hit nearly 61,000 people since January 2025, stealing over $1.6 billion. They call or email pretending to be the FBI, IRS, Social Security, or local police — saying you owe money, your identity was stolen, or there's a warrant. They demand payment by wire, gift card, or crypto.

What to do: Hang up. Government agencies never call demanding money or threatening arrest. If you're worried, look up the real number yourself and call back.…
